newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Yilmaz visits president in govt talks.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Yilmaz visits president in govt talks.

text.p: Turkey's prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz began talks with President Suleyman Demirel on Sunday about the formation of a secularist government, Anatolian news agency said.
Turkish television said main opposition leader Yilmaz might ask the president to approve his planned coalition.
Anatolian agency earlier said the three parties in Yilmaz's alliance were close to agreement on a protocol outlining the coalition's policies and the distribution of cabinet seats.

It said Yilmaz had been expected to ask for presidential approval within a few days. Resignations from the ruling Islamist-led coalition in recent days have given Yilmaz a slim majority in parliament.
Under Turkish law, the president must approve a new government before it goes to a confidence vote within 10 days.
Yilmaz was asked by the president to find a new government after Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, the first Islamist to lead modern Turkey, resigned earlier this month.
